stories.title: Mass shootings over Halloween weekend leave at least 6 dead and dozens injured across US
stories.summary: Experts on violence say Halloween is one of the most dangerous days of the year. Three shootings early on the morning of Nov. 1 left at least four dead and 15 injured in the Deep Ellum neighborhood of Dallas, Texas, officials confirmed on Sunday. The hail of Texas gunfire was part of a wave of violence on Halloween that left at least 24 dead and 94 wounded across the country, according to police statements. The shootings stretched from California to Delaware. They unfolded at night clubs, costume stores, outside stadiums and near college campuses.

more.text: A spate of shootings in nightlife districts and near university campuses across the United States over Halloween weekend left at least six people dead and dozens wounded, with Dallas recording the highest toll. stories.title: Five quick takeaways from historic Mexico GP
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli crowned F1 champion in Mexico as Ferrari faces another internal dilemma Antonelli didn't have his finest qualifying session in Mexico, but from fifth on the grid he benefitted from Russell's slow start to get ahead and shadow the leaders. With neither Russell nor Hamilton winning the race, Antonelli didn't even have to finish the race.
